title: Client status meeting where go-live is only mentioned
purpose: Weekly status with the client on the HR portal migration
objectives: Confirm who signs off user acceptance testing

brief.text: Project: HR portal migration for Alder Insurance (fictional). Our plan says go-live 3 March, subject to UAT sign-off.

sources.title: Migration plan
sources.text: Go-live planned 3 March. UAT runs 10-21 February. Sign-off by the client HR systems owner.

turns.text: Quick status: data migration dry run finished, two mapping issues open.
Good. On go-live, early March still sounds fine to us, we'll see after testing.
Great. For UAT, who signs off on your side?
That would be Ana's team, or maybe the HR systems owner, we haven't decided.
Let's look at the mapping issues now.
Sure, the first one is the cost centre codes for contractors.

mustInclude: States that the go-live date is not agreed (only 'early March, we'll see')
States that the UAT sign-off owner is still undecided between Ana's team and the HR systems owner
Suggests a concrete way to close one of them before the meeting ends
mustNotInclude: Marks the go-live date as agreed
Marks the UAT sign-off owner as confirmed
checkpoints.ideal: Both objectives remain open; propose confirming 3 March conditional on UAT and naming one sign-off owner today.

mustInclude: Connects the undecided sign-off owner to the UAT window (10-21 February) as a schedule risk
mustNotInclude: Invents a new date or owner
checkpoints.ideal: Mention that without an owner before 10 February, UAT sign-off and the 3 March go-live are at risk.
